3º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 5

Daily routines

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Name the actions we do every day
  • Say the time with o'clock and half past
  • Talk about your day with I + verb and the time
  • Put the actions of the day in order with first, then and after that
  • Tell the time with quarter past and quarter to
  • Talk about another person's routine with -s and -es
  • Say how often we do things with always, usually, sometimes and never
  • Plan and describe a healthy routine

Para pensar

Cada mañana haces casi lo mismo: te despiertas, te levantas, te lavas, desayunas… ¿Cómo se llama eso en inglés y cómo lo contarías?

Explicación

1. What is a routine?

A routine is what we do every day, more or less at the same time. We wake up, eat, go to school, play and sleep. Routines help our body: we sleep better and we learn better.

En castellano: daily significa «diario, de cada día». Para hablar de rutinas usamos el presente, que en inglés se llama present simple: «I get up», «I go to school». Es como en español: «me levanto», «voy al cole».

2. Morning actions

In the morning we do these actions: wake up (despertarse), get up (levantarse), have a shower (ducharse), wash my face (lavarme la cara), brush my teeth (lavarme los dientes), get dressed (vestirme), have breakfast (desayunar) and go to school (ir al cole).

Act them out with your class! Mime each action while you say it: «I brush my teeth» (mueve la mano como un cepillo). Ojo: wake up es abrir los ojos y get up es salir de la cama.

3. Afternoon and evening actions

In the afternoon: have lunch (comer), go home (ir a casa), do my homework (hacer los deberes), play with my friends (jugar con mis amigos), go to the park and have a snack (merendar).

In the evening: have a bath (bañarse), have dinner (cenar), watch TV, read a book, put on my pyjamas and go to bed (acostarse). Truco: muchas comidas usan have: have breakfast, have lunch, have dinner.

4. At the weekend

From Monday to Friday we go to school. These are weekdays (días de diario). Saturday and Sunday are the weekend (fin de semana). Our routine is different at the weekend!

  • On weekdays, I get up at half past seven. At the weekend, I get up at nine o'clock.
  • On weekdays, I have a quick breakfast. On Sundays, I have pancakes with my family.
  • On weekdays, I go to school. On Saturdays, I play football in the park.

Look at the prepositions: at the weekend, on Saturday(s), on Sunday(s). With the -s (on Saturdays), it means every Saturday.

Weekend activities: visit my grandparents, go to the cinema, go swimming, watch a film, play with friends, go to the beach, help at home, sleep late (dormir hasta tarde).

Activity: write three sentences about your weekdays and three about your weekend.

5. What time is it? O'clock

To say the time, ask: What time is it? (¿qué hora es?). When the long hand points to 12, we say o'clock (en punto): «It's seven o'clock», «It's three o'clock».

To say when we do something, use at: «I get up at seven o'clock», «I have lunch at two o'clock». En castellano: «a las siete» se dice «at seven». No hace falta poner «the»: nunca digas «at the seven».

6. Half past

When the long hand points to 6, half an hour has passed. In English we say half past (y media) + the hour: «It's half past eight» (las ocho y media), «I go to school at half past eight».

Ojo: en inglés el orden es «media pasada de las ocho». Para practicar, mira un reloj de verdad cada media hora y di la hora en voz alta: «It's half past four! Time for a snack!».

7. Quarter past and quarter to

An hour has 60 minutes. Half an hour is 30 minutes. And a quarter (un cuarto) is 15 minutes.

  • Quarter past (y cuarto): the long hand is on the 3. «It's quarter past eight.» (8:15)
  • Quarter to (menos cuarto): the long hand is on the 9. «It's quarter to nine.» (8:45)

Look carefully! With quarter to, we say the next hour: 8:45 is quarter to nine, like in Spanish: las nueve menos cuarto.

Let's review all the times with the hour 4:

  • 4:00 – four o'clock
  • 4:15 – quarter past four
  • 4:30 – half past four
  • 4:45 – quarter to five

To ask: «What time is it?» To talk about routines: «What time do you have lunch?» – «At quarter past two.» Use at with times.

Activity: draw four clocks and write the time under each one.

8. My day in sentences

Now join the action and the time: I + action + at + time. «I wake up at seven o'clock. I have breakfast at half past seven. I go to school at half past eight. I have lunch at two o'clock. I go to bed at nine o'clock.»

Use in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening and at night for parts of the day: «I do my homework in the afternoon.» «I read a book at night.»

9. He gets up, she has breakfast

When we talk about another person (he, she, my mum, Ana), the verb changes: we add -s.

  • I get up → She gets up.
  • I wake up → He wakes up.
  • I go to bed → My dad goes to bed.

Some verbs add -es: verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -o, -ss:

  • brush → brushes: «He brushes his teeth.»
  • watch → watches: «She watches TV.»
  • go → goes, do → does: «He does his homework.»

And there is one special verb: have → has. «She has breakfast at eight.»

Look at the change in the words my and his/her too: «I brush my teeth.» → «He brushes his teeth.» / «She brushes her teeth.»

Activity: write five sentences about the routine of a person in your family. Underline the -s.

10. First, then, after that

To tell your routine in order, use sequence words: First (primero), then (luego), after that (después de eso) and finally (por último).

«First, I get up. Then, I wash my face. After that, I get dressed and have breakfast. Finally, I go to school.» These words make your text clear and easy to follow. Ponlas al principio de la frase y después una coma.

11. How often? Always, sometimes, never

To say how often (con qué frecuencia) we do something, we use these words:

  • always (siempre) – 100 %: «I always brush my teeth.»
  • usually (normalmente) – 80 %: «I usually walk to school.»
  • sometimes (a veces) – 50 %: «I sometimes watch TV after dinner.»
  • never (nunca) – 0 %: «I never go to bed late on weekdays.»

Look at the position: these words go before the action verb: «She always gets up at seven.» But they go after am, is, are: «I am always happy on Fridays.»

Be careful with never: it is already negative. We say «I never eat sweets», not I don't never.

To ask: «How often do you…?» – «Every day.» / «Twice a week.» (dos veces por semana)

Activity: write one sentence with each word about your routine.

12. Reading: Ana's Saturday

Read: «On Saturdays my routine is different! I wake up at nine o'clock. First, I have a big breakfast with my family: pancakes! Then, at half past ten, I go to the swimming pool with my dad. After that, I have lunch at my grandma's house at two o'clock. In the afternoon I play with my cousins in the park. I have dinner at eight o'clock and I go to bed at half past nine.»

Answer: What time does Ana wake up? Where does she have lunch?

13. School days in the UK and in Spain

Children around the world have different routines. Let's compare a school day in the UK and in Spain.

In the UK:

  • Children usually start school at about quarter to nine.
  • They wear a school uniform in most schools.
  • They have lunch at school at about twelve o'clock, often a packed lunch (comida de casa en una fiambrera).
  • School usually finishes at about quarter past three.
  • They have dinner early, at about six o'clock.

In Spain:

  • Many children start school at nine o'clock.
  • Lunch is often the big meal of the day, at about two o'clock.
  • Many children do after-school activities (extraescolares).
  • Dinner is late, at about nine o'clock!

Which routine do you prefer? Why?

Activity: compare your school day with a British school day in three sentences.

14. Let's practise: my routine clock

Make a routine clock. Draw a big circle on a card and divide it into parts: morning, afternoon, evening and night. In each part, draw what you do and write the sentence: «I have lunch at two o'clock».

Then interview a partner: «What time do you get up?» — «I get up at half past seven.» «What time do you go to bed?» — «At nine o'clock.» Compare: ¿quién se levanta antes? ¿Quién duerme más horas?

15. Digital time: seven fifteen

On a digital clock (reloj digital), on a phone or on a train timetable (horario), we see numbers: 7:15. In English we can read them in two ways:

  • 7:15 – «quarter past seven» or «seven fifteen»
  • 7:30 – «half past seven» or «seven thirty»
  • 7:45 – «quarter to eight» or «seven forty-five»
  • 7:05 – «seven oh five» (we say oh for the zero)

The digital way is easy: we just say the hour and then the minutes. Remember the tens: ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty.

We also use a.m. for the morning (from midnight to midday) and p.m. for the afternoon and evening: «I get up at 7 a.m. I go to bed at 9 p.m.»

Activity: read these times in two ways: 6:30, 9:15, 11:45, 2:05.

16. A healthy routine

A good routine helps us feel healthy and happy. Here are some tips for children:

  • Sleep well: children need about ten hours of sleep every night. Go to bed at the same time every day.
  • Have breakfast: it gives you energy for the morning.
  • Wash your hands before meals and brush your teeth twice a day.
  • Move: play outside, walk, ride a bike or do sport every day.
  • Screens (pantallas): don't use the tablet or TV just before bed.
  • Read: a story before bed helps you relax.

We can write tips with should (deberías): «You should sleep ten hours.» «You shouldn't eat sweets every day.»

A healthy routine is not boring: it gives you time for school, play, family and rest.

Activity: make a poster called «My healthy routine» with six tips and drawings.

My daily routine

Ejercicios

  1. Traduce: levantarse, vestirse, desayunar.

  2. ¿Cómo se dice «cenar»?

  3. ¿Cómo se dice «hacer los deberes»?

  4. Escribe en inglés: 9:00.

  5. Escribe en inglés: 2:30.

  6. Completa: «I go to bed ___ nine o'clock.»

  7. Completa: «I do my homework in the ___.» (tarde)

  8. Pregunta a qué hora se levanta tu amigo.

  9. Ordena con First, Then, Finally: ir al cole, desayunar, levantarse.

  10. Escribe tres frases de tu rutina con la hora.

  11. How do you say «fin de semana» in English?

  12. Write 3:15 in words.

  13. Complete: «She ___ (have) breakfast at eight.»

  14. What does «never» mean?

  15. In the reading, what does Sam do?

  16. Write 10:45 in words.

  17. Change to «she»: «I brush my teeth.»

  18. Order: always / up / I / seven / get / at

  19. What time does Sam start work?

  20. Translate: Normalmente voy andando al colegio.

  21. What do the animals at the zoo eat in the reading?

  22. Write five sentences about Sam's day with he and -s.

  23. Compare your school day with a British school day.

  24. Write six tips for a healthy routine with should.

Practica

  1. «Levantarse» is…

    1. A) go to bed
    2. B) get up
    3. C) get dressed

  2. «Lavarse los dientes» is…

    1. A) brush my teeth
    2. B) wash my teeth
    3. C) clean my mouth

  3. «Cenar» is…

    1. A) have lunch
    2. B) have breakfast
    3. C) have dinner

  4. 7:00 is…

    1. A) half past seven
    2. B) seven half
    3. C) seven o'clock

  5. 6:30 is…

    1. A) half past six
    2. B) six o'clock
    3. C) half past seven

  6. I get up ___ eight o'clock.

    1. A) in
    2. B) at
    3. C) on

  7. I do my homework ___ the afternoon.

    1. A) in
    2. B) at
    3. C) on

  8. «Primero» is…

    1. A) then
    2. B) finally
    3. C) first

  9. «Por último» is…

    1. A) first
    2. B) finally
    3. C) after

  10. «What time is it?» means…

    1. A) ¿qué tiempo hace?
    2. B) ¿qué hora es?
    3. C) ¿cuánto tiempo?

  11. 8:45 is…

    1. A) quarter past eight
    2. B) quarter to nine
    3. C) quarter to eight

  12. «He ___ his homework.»

    1. A) do
    2. B) dos
    3. C) does

  13. «A veces» in English is…

    1. A) always
    2. B) sometimes
    3. C) usually

  14. «I go to the park ___ Saturdays.»

    1. A) on
    2. B) at
    3. C) in

  15. How many hours do children need to sleep?

    1. A) about five
    2. B) about fifteen
    3. C) about ten

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué es una rutina diaria; Qué acciones hago por la mañana, la tarde y la noche; Cómo digo la hora con o'clock y half past; Cómo cuento mi día en orden con first, then y finally.

Zookeeper

Healthy
